descriptions.text: - In the _withdrawFrom function, the value liabilityToBurn is determined by the asset.liability and asset.totalSupply. However, the actual exchange/swap process is using the oracle as price feed. This introduces inconsistency for arbitrage. - Attacker could deposit USDT token, swap them to USDCE using oracle price(however the liability is influenced), but during the withdraw process which uses asset liability, the attacker could get back more assets than the original deposit tokens. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack tx: https://arbiscan.io/tx/0x57c96e320a3b885fabd95dd476d43c0d0fb10500d940d9594d4a458471a87abe Analysis: https://twitter.com/AnciliaInc/status/1712676040471105870 https://twitter.com/CertiKAlert/status/1712707006979613097

The Beluga Protocol on Arbitrum fell victim to a flashloan attack. The attacker made a profit of approximately $175,000 by manipulating the USDT-USDC.e balance, allowing for the withdrawal of extra tokens.

Beluga on Arbitrum One was exploited on 13 October 2023 via manipulated stablecoin pool pricing, resulting in losses around $175,000 USD. The attacker used flash loans to alter pool balances, enabling inflated withdrawals before repaying the loan. The stable swap pool contract relied on spot AMM balances as the basis for asset pricing and withdrawal logic. The attacker used flash loaned stablecoins to manipulate these balances, inflating their redeemable amount and extracting extra tokens. No time-weighted or manipulation-resistant oracle supported collateral or settlement prices.
